proofUses.reason: The susceptibility identity is solved with the correct minus sign. Fourier positivity and a positive numerator establish positivity of the effective reciprocal.
An exact quotient-product identity and absolute-kernel increment bounds give an explicit improving estimate. Positivity is proved before applying the reciprocal lemma.
Continuity of all three suprema and a pointwise weak-to-strong implication close the argument without assuming a global weak bound.
Spatial monotone convergence supplies the critical triangle. Coefficient norm convergence, a positive denominator bound and integrable domination then justify the critical Fourier density.

An explicit pointwise improvement closes by continuity for d>=10^11. Critical coefficient convergence and Fourier domination supply every hypothesis of the sixth-norm spatial theorem, without invoking an unspecified dimension threshold.

Actual deleted-bond coefficient diagrams and weighted witness estimates supply separate mass and frequency errors. The canonical Fourier equation, positivity and reciprocal second differences give a pointwise improvement from two to 17/10; actual finite-susceptibility continuity removes the weak premise.

The actual coefficient normalization bounds open-step mass by d/(d−44). The inequality p(beta)≥beta/(2d+beta) converts this to the intensity bound, and sharpness identifies the supremum of finite-susceptibility intensities with the percolation threshold.

The closed subcritical bootstrap gives the explicit continuation bound. Actual two-point left continuity and finite partial sums of nonnegative diagrams preserve it at the finite critical endpoint, without assuming critical cluster finiteness.
The subcritical first-step expansion has no direct-step contribution at zero. Pass its sharper continuation estimate to criticality using the same nonnegative partial-sum limit.
The exact origin comparison Δ≤1+(3/2)T(0) turns the improved critical continuation estimate into the stated full triangle constant.

Actual boundary Russo identities and finite-cluster moment bounds give the positive-part-square susceptibility derivative below the endpoint. Integrate for chi-D and retain the maximum of the affine numerator endpoint values; transitivity gives every root.

The actual stopped-exploration comparison bounds the infinite-cluster probability at b by (b-beta)² chi_beta/beta. The reciprocal susceptibility estimate makes this tend to zero; a countable intersection gives simultaneous all-root finiteness.
Self-avoiding path counting and positive percolation above the actual threshold give the lower probability bound. Continuity passes j≤d/(d−44) to the endpoint, giving the upper bound.

Critical pair-state bounds give initial mass at most 1+8882/(315d), transfer mass at most 1/855 and terminal mass at most 1/1712. All critical clusters, and hence deleted clusters, are finite almost surely. Apply the canonical infinite equation using the actual finite continuation bound.

Pass the actual subcritical mass normalization to the endpoint. The coefficient transform converges by signed-kernel norm continuity and the walk parameter tends to one by divergent critical susceptibility.

The canonical subcritical quotient, continuity of step mass and signed-kernel norm continuity give numerator and denominator limits. The improved actual model bounds keep the critical denominator positive off the singular set.
Pass the improved subcritical infrared bound to the quotient limit, with the walk parameter tending to one. Positive numerator and denominator give strict positivity.

The reciprocal symbol deficit is integrable. Dominated convergence in the actual subcritical inverse formula, together with pointwise spatial continuity, identifies the critical inverse Fourier coefficients.
Pass the actual subcritical second-difference bound to the three quotient limits and to the walk majorant limit. The four explicit nonsingularity conditions justify each reciprocal limit.
